{{verse|chapter=1|verse=1|align=float}}{{dropinitial|T}}{{sc|He}} Seniour to Gaius the deere{{ls}}t, whom I loue in truth. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=2|align=float}}† My deere{{ls}}t, concerning al thinges I make my praier that thou proceede pro{{ls}}perou{{ls}}ly, and fare vvel, as thy {{ls}}oule doth pro{{ls}}perou{{ls}}ly. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=3|align=float}}† I vvas exceding glad vvhen the brethren came, and gaue te{{ls}}timonie to thy truth, euen as thou vvalke{{ls}}t in truth. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=4|align=float}}† Greater {{outside R|''`plea{{ls}}ure:'' {{lang|grc|χαρὰν}}.}}`thanke' haue I not of them, then that I may heare my children do vvalke in truth. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=5|align=float}}† My deere{{ls}}t, thou doe{{ls}}t faithfully vvhat{{ls}}oeuer thou vvorke{{ls}}t on the brethren, ∷ {{outside L|∷ A great grace to be beneficial to {{ls}}trangers, {{ls}}pecially to them that be of our Catholike faith and {{ls}}uffer for the {{ls}}ame.}} and that vpon {{ls}}trangers. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=6|align=float}}† they haue rendred te{{ls}}timonie to thy charitie in the {{ls}}ight of the Church: vvhō, thou {{ls}}halt doe vvel, bringing on their vvay in maner vvorthie of God. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=7|align=float}}† For, for his name did they depart, taking nothing<noinclude>{{continues|of}}
